country_context.note: This profile concerns Japanese in Japan and does not imply that all speakers use one identical accent or register.

coverage_targets: Tokyo standard accent and pitch-accent notation
regional pitch-accent systems and lexical differences
phonemic length, mora timing, devoicing, gemination, and contracted speech
regional accents including Kansai, Tohoku, Kyushu, and Okinawan-area Japanese
politeness levels and honorific/humble forms
plain versus polite speech
sentence-final particles and conversational stance
age, relationship, workplace, service, and regional context
標準語 and 共通語 distinctions where relevant
modern standard grammar and orthography
kanji, kana, and common written conventions
formal, academic, workplace, and public-facing registers
colloquial contractions and omitted particles
youth slang and internet expressions with date/context labels
regional vocabulary and Kansai conversational forms
gendered and generational stereotypes must not be presented as universal rules
insults and dismissive expressions
coarse language and taboo expressions
differences in force by relationship, intonation, and situation
neutral Indonesian meaning, severity, and likely social effect
Ainu language and communities
Ryukyuan languages: Amami, Kunigami, Okinawan, Miyako, Yaeyama, and Yonaguni
Hachijo and regional Japonic varieties
Do not flatten distinct languages into a generic Japanese dialect label

sources.title: Agency for Cultural Affairs: Japanese Language Policy and Endangered Languages and Dialects
